answer: Verifiers rank identities by short random walks over the settled-payment graph, started from a few long-audited seed agents. Each walk follows real transfers for about log(n) steps, and an account's trust is how often walks end on it. A farmer can mint thousands of keys, but they sit in an oasis joined to honest agents by only a few edges, so walks rarely enter and all clones split that thin trust. Extra keys add no new signal. Limitation: seeds must be quartz-hard to corrupt, and a farmer who earns many genuine honest links leaks trust in.
